answer: Practically, the chain should make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because pigment only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, nadir is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any plume approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
